title: Arjuna's austerities
hook: in Indra's city, Urvashi comes to Arjuna's door at night, and he covers his eyes
carry: pause once before you follow it

segments.voice: Yesterday: Arjuna's austerities paid off: healing, the Pashupata with its warning, and weapons from the guardians of the world. Your line was use only as much as you need.

Arjuna is living in heaven. His brothers are still in the forest, and he is in Indra's city, learning the weapons of the gods. Indra has him learn music and dance as well, from the gandharva Chitrasena. Then one evening Indra notices how Arjuna's eyes follow the apsara Urvashi, and he sends word to her. So that night, dressed for him, she comes to his door. And the archer who fought a hunter who turned out to be Shiva does something Urvashi doesn't expect. He covers his eyes.
screen: `ARJUNA IN INDRA'S CITY.` → `URVASHI AT THE DOOR.` → `HE COVERS HIS EYES.`

segments.voice: In the telling, Arjuna speaks to her with great respect, and what he says surprises her. You are an elder of my own line, he tells her. Tradition says Urvashi was the mother of an ancestor of the Pandavas' house, so to Arjuna she stands where Kunti stands, or Indra's queen. He looked at her in the hall, he says, the way a child looks at an honored elder. Urvashi answers that the apsaras are free; rules like his don't bind them. He doesn't move. And she is furious. She curses him: he will live among women as a dancer, without his manhood, and be thought little of. Arjuna goes to Chitrasena, and the story reaches Indra. Here it turns. Indra isn't angry. He's pleased. He praises Arjuna's self-control, and tells him the curse will serve him. When the brothers must live hidden, unrecognized, he will spend that time as a dancer among women, and no one will look for the great archer there. When that time is over, the curse is over too. On the mountain, austerity meant fasting, standing, enduring. Here it's a door, a night, and a no: the same discipline, carried into a palace full of pleasures. The epic doesn't treat the curse as a reward for virtue, exactly. It's something stranger: a wound that becomes a hiding place. He went up for weapons. He comes down with weapons, a teacher's music, and a disguise he doesn't know he'll need.
screen: `"YOU ARE AN ELDER OF MY LINE."` · `URVASHI'S CURSE.` · `INDRA: IT WILL HIDE YOU.` · then, large: `AUSTERITY CARRIED INTO A PALACE.`

segments.voice: When a small pull comes as you sit, to shift, to scratch, to check the time, don't fight it and don't follow it. Notice it rise, the way Arjuna noticed the knock at the door, and let it pass like a breath going out; if you pray, offer each small no as part of your prayer.
Arjuna's austerities. They began on a mountain with fasting and ended in a palace with a closed door, and a curse that would one day hide him.
Your line: pause once before you follow it. Arjuna's austerities end not on a mountain, but at a closed door. That's day seven hundred eighty-seven.

howItsDone: The episode of Urvashi and Arjuna is told within the Vana Parva of the Mahabharata, and retellers often pair it with the later year in disguise, when the curse becomes Arjuna's cover.

chat.says: Why did Arjuna turn Urvashi away when she came to his door?
options: He saw her as an elder of his own line, like a mother, and treated her with respect.
He was afraid Indra would be angry with him for being with an apsara.
He had taken a lifelong vow never to marry, like his great-uncle Bhishma.
chat.meaning: Tradition says Urvashi was mother of an ancestor of the Pandavas' house, so Arjuna saw her as an honored elder, like Kunti.

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli that Indra sends Chitrasena to Urvashi after noticing Arjuna's gaze, and that Arjuna covers his eyes when she arrives.
Arjuna's reason (Urvashi as mother of the Puru/Kuru line through Pururavas and Ayus) is softened to 'tradition says ... an ancestor'; confirm phrasing.
Indra limits the curse to the period of hiding; Ganguli gives a length in years. Left without a number under the claims rule.
Assumes days 782–786 covered the departure, the mountain, the Kirata, the Pashupata and arrival in Indra's city; if any of them already told the Urvashi episode, reangle this day.
The practice frames restraint as noticing a pull; no prayer is written.
